issues.description: raise PerformanceWarning is wrong control flow; warnings should be warned, not raised
issues.detail: The code does `raise PerformanceWarning(msg)` which turns a warning class into a hard exception. The test confirms this with `pytest.raises(PerformanceWarning, ...)`. PerformanceWarning is a Warning subclass and the convention (and the rest of dask) is `warnings.warn(msg, PerformanceWarning)`. Raising it breaks the meaning of the type and silently changes the API contract; users with a too-small chunk-size config will get an exception instead of a warning plus a safe write. Pick one: either warn and continue with shard-aligned chunks, or raise a real Exception with a clear name. Don't conflate them.

issues.description: Unreachable break after raise; dead code reveals confused intent
issues.detail: Inside the `if not nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw == 0:` block, `raise PerformanceWarning(msg)` is immediately followed by `break`. The break can never execute. This is a smell that the author was uncertain whether to raise, warn, or just continue, and the data structure of the check (per-axis loop, single global decision) was never nailed down. Decide the shape: is this a per-axis check that aggregates, or a fail-fast on first bad axis? Then write it that way.

issues.description: safe_chunk_size computation uses prod of chunks tuple, not bytes-of-one-shard; likely wrong number in the message
issues.detail: `safe_chunk_size = np.prod(zarr_write_chunks) * max(1, z.dtype.itemsize)`. `zarr_write_chunks` is a tuple of tuples returned by `_get_zarr_write_chunks` shaped for normalize_chunks (e.g. `((12,), (12,), ...)` style), not a flat shape tuple. np.prod over a tuple-of-tuples will either misbehave or produce a value with the wrong meaning. The number printed to the user as 'at least N bytes' will be incorrect or confusing. Compute it from the actual shard shape (the scalar per-axis values) times itemsize, and add a test that asserts the exact number in the message for a known shape.

issues.description: Per-axis divisibility check uses dw[0] only; assumes uniform chunks, silently wrong on uneven tails
issues.detail: `nominal_dask_chunk_size = dw[0]` looks only at the first chunk in the axis. After normalize_chunks with auto, the last chunk on an axis is commonly a smaller remainder. Checking only dw[0] % zw is a half-truth: dw[0] can be aligned while a later element isn't, or vice versa for tiny arrays. The right data structure here is 'is every interior chunk a multiple of zw' or equivalently 'is the nominal/auto chunk a multiple of zw'. Make the predicate match the data shape; right now the code is fighting the tuple.

issues.description: The whole block wants to be a small filter: (zarr_write_chunks, dask_write_chunks) -> aligned_chunks_or_error
issues.detail: COULD-BE-A-FILTER. The validation/alignment logic is woven into to_zarr inline, with an unreachable break and ambiguous raise-vs-warn semantics. Lift it into a single function `_align_dask_chunks_to_shards(dask_chunks, zarr_write_chunks, dtype) -> tuple[chunks, Optional[Warning]]` (or that raises a named exception). to_zarr then becomes: compute zarr_write_chunks, ask the filter for aligned dask chunks, rechunk. The data flow becomes obvious and the test surface shrinks to one function instead of one end-to-end path per region variant.

issues.description: Error message tells user to set chunk-size to shard bytes, but doesn't explain that the global config is the source of the conflict
issues.detail: The PR description explicitly notes the misalignment only happens when `array.chunk-size` is smaller than the shard. The message hints at this but buries the lede. Lead with the cause ('Your dask config array.chunk-size of X bytes is smaller than the Zarr shard size of Y bytes'), then the remedy. Right now users will read the message, set the suggested number, and not understand why.

issues.description: `if not nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw == 0` reads worse than `if nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw != 0`
issues.detail: Operator precedence makes this parse correctly but it forces the reader to think about it. The simpler version is one token shorter and unambiguous. Small thing, but this is a 30-line block doing one job; make every line trivial to read.

issues.description: `if len(dw) >= 1` is effectively always true for a non-empty array; dead guard
issues.detail: normalize_chunks returns at least one chunk per axis for any non-degenerate shape. The guard either protects nothing or protects a zero-shape case that the rest of the function doesn't handle anyway. Drop it or replace with an explicit precondition.

issues.description: Test asserts existence of warning behavior via pytest.raises, codifying the wrong contract
issues.detail: `test_zarr_risky_shards_warns` uses `pytest.raises(PerformanceWarning, ...)`. If the raise-vs-warn issue (P0 above) is fixed, this test will need to switch to `pytest.warns`. Worth fixing together so the test name ('warns') and assertion ('raises') stop disagreeing.

review.summary: The data structures and overall direction are right: use shard shape as previous_chunks, let auto pick a shard-aligned multiple, validate alignment, fall through cleanly for the region path. The new test parametrization is a real improvement. But the validation block is muddled: it raises a class named PerformanceWarning (should be warned, or renamed to a real exception), has an unreachable break after the raise, checks only dw[0] for divisibility, and computes safe_chunk_size from a tuple-of-tuples in a way that probably prints the wrong number. Lift the alignment logic into one small filter function — (dask_chunks, zarr_write_chunks, dtype) in, (aligned_chunks, optional_warning_or_raise) out — and the to_zarr call site becomes three obvious lines. Fix the raise/warn contract before merge; the rest is cleanup.
